pillar_reactions.evidence: Presented in the lower-tier form, not the one-to-one form: self-directed programmes, a three-to-four-session week that can be split two-and-two, monthly changing challenges, mobility protocols, and community form review rather than coach form review. Brent's response to the whole block was 'Sounds interesting.' No questions and no tie-back to his own knee or mobility goals. He had pre-endorsed the modality before the pitch — 'I ran into Trevor's videos and I thought that would be cool to mix into my schedule' — so acceptance here says little.

Presented as protocol-not-calorie-counting, mainly whole foods, with drinks and pizza explicitly permitted. Brent gave no reaction at all to the nutrition portion of the lower-tier pitch. Earlier in discovery he had accepted the premise willingly when pressed on weekend drinking — 'I think I can adapt a little bit to it' — and had diagnosed himself: 'I think probably the drinking is nutrition-wise the biggest hurdle.' The specific thing he asked for, 'some tips on how to change my nutrition', is narrower than what was described.

Delivered as community accountability rather than one-to-one: posting progress, seeing others progress, filming form and posting it for Trevor or another member to correct. Accepted without comment. Notable that the one-to-one version of this pillar was described separately and explicitly declined by the prospect in favour of the self-directed tier — asked which of the two he leaned toward, he first said 'I'm not sure about the difference about the two you mentioned', and on clarification chose the self-directed one immediately: 'Oh, that's more the one I'm looking for.'

anchors.raw: I'm doing strength training for, I think, three years now... I quite like it, but it's really, yeah, how do you explain it? Strength focused and not really functional... It's not that I want to quit regular gymming for 100%
anchors.note: The strongest anchor here and an unusual one: not a cheaper competitor but an incumbent solution that is working. He tracks his lifts, is happy with his strength progress, and wants an addition rather than a replacement. Everything the six-month transformation charges for, he believes he already has most of.

anchors.raw: Yeah. The price doesn't really shock me, to be honest. It's something that I would expect from a schedule like it.
anchors.note: Explicitly supportive and volunteered in response to 'at least like in the four figures'. He then also absorbed $2,000/year without a flicker. Price was never the obstacle on this call; scope was. Worth recording because it is the counterexample to the assumption that non-buyers are price-driven.

anchors.raw: my physiotherapist recommended me to do something like kettlebell lunges, or more functional movements to improve my knee stability a little bit
anchors.note: He already pays for professional physical guidance and acts on it, and that clinician independently endorsed the modality being sold. A strong, entirely unused supportive anchor — the rep never connected the physio's recommendation to the offer.

anchors.raw: But then I started to try it out a little bit, the training... And then I thought, okay, maybe it's better if I just book a meeting to do it properly instead of finding it out myself.
anchors.note: He has already been self-serving from the free content and got far enough with it to want to formalise. The paid tier has to beat free content he is already using successfully, and the tier he was offered — a self-directed programme library — is the closest thing to it.

unmet_demand.want: A review of his existing gym split with kettlebell sessions blended into it — 'someone to review my current training and say, okay, I would maybe change this, this, and this. And on day A, you can do kettlebell training, do these exercises on day two as well. But yeah, still with my current gym schedule mixed into it.'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The rep said combining with the gym 'is always possible' but then disqualified the coach from doing it: 'he isn't like an expert in the gym, like he's not a personal trainer or anything.' Neither product is a programming consult on someone else's training. This is the clearest, most specifically articulated product gap in the batch and the prospect stated it unprompted.

unmet_demand.want: A low-commitment way to test whether kettlebell training suits him before buying a transformation — 'it's more like a trying out thing... maybe later on I would be open to do like a full package thing, but it's not really what I'm looking for right now.'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Partially served — this is exactly what the $2,000/year or $200/month tier is for, and the rep routed him there. Left recorded because the tier is undocumented, unnamed on the call, and the two prices do not reconcile, so what he is being asked to try is not clearly defined.

unmet_demand.want: Training that works around and rehabilitates a healing meniscus tear, in line with what his physiotherapist has already advised.
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Never addressed. The rep noted the joints were 'locked up' and moved on; the product he was sold has no individual programming and no coach reviewing his knee. Whether a self-directed loaded programme is appropriate at 60-70% leg capacity six weeks or so post-injury was not asked and is not known from this call.
